cases.title: Escape must close the suggestion list without erasing what the user typed
cases.summary: Pressing Escape to dismiss suggestions sets the input value to an empty string, so a user editing a saved field loses their text.
cases.status: Open. The maintainer tracks the change for v11 in issue #485; no fix is merged at pinnedCommit (the current head).

review.reviewer: Project author, after the browser verdict. This is a reading of the patch, not another test.
review.summary: The one line that set the input to an empty string on Escape is removed; Escape still closes the list. This is the default the maintainer proposes in #485.
caveats: The clear event is still emitted on Escape although nothing is cleared any more; listeners for it may now be misleading.
#485 also proposes a clearOnEscape option for the old behaviour; an upstream pull request would need to add it.

cases.expectedBehaviour: As proposed by the maintainer in #485: Escape closes the list only and keeps the input. The reporter of #402 suggested restoring the earlier value instead; this task follows the maintainer's plan.

cases.title: Passing through a prefilled datepicker must not change the date the form submits
cases.summary: The datepicker instance is created on focusin and immediately rewrites the input with a locale string, so a saved 2026-10-22 is submitted as 10/22/2026 although the user never picked a date.
cases.status: Open. Fixes are proposed in pull requests #43150 and #43151, not merged at pinnedCommit. They are never sent to the model.

pendingHumanCheck.applied: js/src changes only (tests and docs omitted)
pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix passes the same frozen task. It was fetched for comparison and is never part of a model request.

review.reviewer: Project author, after the browser verdict. This is a reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Works, different trade-off from the pending human fix
review.summary: The input now keeps the ISO date of the selection instead of the locale-formatted string.
caveats: An input-mode datepicker now shows 2026-10-22 rather than the localized date.
Pending pull request #43150 keeps the localized text visible and submits the ISO date through a hidden input. Both pass this task; the human design is the better user experience.

cases.expectedBehaviour: Only the part of the issue every proposal agrees on: focusing and leaving the field without picking keeps the submitted value 2026-10-22. What a newly picked date should submit is still being decided upstream and is not tested.

cases.title: Tab must leave a datepicker input for the next field
cases.summary: When the field is reached with Tab, the calendar does not open, but vanilla-calendar-pro treats it as shown: on the next Tab it cancels the key and focuses the first control of a calendar that is not in the page, so focus stays in the date field. Escape is the only way out, and it drops focus to the page body.
cases.status: Not found among Bootstrap's open or closed issues when pinned. Reproduced in headless Chromium 156 and in desktop Chrome 155, both with this source and with the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 bundle and stylesheet. Not yet reported upstream.

review.reviewer: Project author, after the browser verdict. This is a reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Rejected on review: it breaks the calendar
review.summary: The patch passes input mode as false to vanilla-calendar-pro. That removes the Tab trap, but after a click the calendar is no longer visible (0 of 35 days visible, against 35 before the patch).
caveats: The frozen pointer path never opened the calendar, so the browser gate could not see this.
A stricter case, bootstrap6-datepicker-tab-trap-with-picker, adds a pointer guard for it; the patch is replayed there without inference.

cases.expectedBehaviour: With the calendar closed, Tab moves to the next field (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap). When the calendar is open, for example after a click, Tab moving into it is the library's intended design and is not changed by this task. Escape keeps closing the calendar.

cases.title: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open however often Escape is pressed
cases.summary: keyboard: false only calls preventDefault() on the native cancel event. Escape does not count as user activation, so after a few presses Chromium fires cancel with cancelable=false and the dialog closes anyway.
cases.status: Open and labelled confirmed. A maintainer-side fix is proposed in pull request #43077, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model; it is kept for comparison after it merges.

pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix passes the same frozen task. It was fetched for comparison and is never part of a model request.

review.reviewer: Project author, after the browser verdict. This is a reading of the patch, not another test.
review.verdict: Sound, and close to the pending human fix
review.summary: Nemotron diagnosed that the cancel event becomes non-cancelable, and now cancels the Escape keydown whenever keyboard is false, for modal dialogs too, so no close request is sent. Pending pull request #43077 makes the same change.
caveats: The human fix also plays the static-backdrop bounce on each press for modal dialogs and keeps the cancel handler as a fallback for close requests that do not come from a key; the model patch does neither.
Version 5 failed this case three times. The difference in version 6 is the key trace, which shows cancel arriving with cancelable=false.

cases.title: Opening a drawer must move keyboard focus into it
cases.summary: A closed drawer is visibility: hidden and becomes visible through the slide-in transition. showModal() runs its focusing steps while everything inside is still hidden, so focus falls back to body and the trigger behind the modal is inert.
cases.status: Open, labelled confirmed and needs-decision. A fix is proposed in pull request #43139, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model.

pendingHumanCheck.note: The pending human fix changes scss/_drawer.scss. This case serves the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 stylesheet, so the SCSS change was not compiled or checked here.

review.reviewer: Project author, after the browser verdict. This is a reading of the attempts, not another test.
review.summary: Ultra now looked for the drawer dismiss button generically ([data-bs-dismiss="drawer"]) instead of naming the test page, but focused it while the drawer was still visibility: hidden, so focus stayed on body.
caveats: A working repair has to move focus once the slide-in transition has made the content visible.
The version 5 run passed this case only by hardcoding the page id #filters-close; version 6 rejects that, and this honest failure replaces the earlier pass.
Pending pull request #43139 fixes it in the stylesheet, which this case cannot edit.

cases.expectedBehaviour: Focus lands on the first focusable control in the drawer, its close button, as for a native modal dialog. The compiled stylesheet is a dependency outside the editable source, so a repair has to be made in the TypeScript.

cases.title: Arrow keys must not select a day that disableDayFn closes
cases.summary: A disabled day cannot be clicked, but ArrowRight from Friday selects the closed Saturday and the form submits it.
cases.status: Open since July 2025 and confirmed by a second user. The repository was archived, so no upstream fix will ship.
cases.expectedBehaviour: Author decision: the arrow key moves to the next day that is not disabled, as when a user skips over closed days with the pointer.

cases.title: Tab after typing a date must move to the next field, not jump back into the date field
cases.summary: Typing a date and pressing Tab fires change; Pikaday redraws and, one millisecond later, focuses the date field again, so the next field loses focus and the user's typing lands in the wrong place.
cases.status: Open since January 2019. The repository was archived, so no upstream fix will ship.
